m3.$description: Semantic aliases for the Android app: the Material 3 ColorScheme roles. Like the Tailwind layer, every token here is a pure alias — the generator refuses anything else, because a literal in this file would be a second palette. Slots whose value references {color.accent}, {color.accent-2} or {color.on-accent} are re-resolved per CopyPasteAccent at runtime; the rest are theme constants. A `composeAlpha` extension means the slot is that colour at that alpha, which is how the tint-based containers (v1 has no opaque container colours) cross over.

primaryContainer.$description: M3 wants a low-emphasis accent surface; --accent-2 is the accent ramp's light step.

secondaryContainer.$description: The accent-tinted selection fill. M3 uses secondaryContainer for the selected NavigationBar/NavigationRail item, which is exactly what v1's --selected does for .sb__item.on and .row.sel. Same alpha as the desktop: 16% dark, 12% light.

tertiary.$description: M3 requires a third accent role that CopyPaste does not have. It aliases the accent-2 ramp step rather than introducing a hue we would then have to maintain.

surface.$description: M3 `surface` is the chrome surface — app bar, navigation bar. Maps to --panel, matching the desktop sidebar and title bar.

surfaceTint.$description: The hue M3 mixes into elevated surfaces. Following the accent keeps tonal elevation on-brand.

inverseSurface.$description: M3 inverts to the text colour; --text is by construction the maximum-contrast surface in either theme.

errorContainer.$description: v1's .btn--danger is a 16% --err tint, not an opaque container. Reproduced here at the same alpha so a Material error surface matches the desktop danger button.

onErrorContainer.$description: The AA-corrected variant from §8.3, which exists precisely because --err fails AA as small text on its own tint. Using --err here would reintroduce the bug §8.3 fixed.

surfaceDim.$description: The surfaceContainer ramp below is the direct Material 3 equivalent of the desktop shadow ramp: Android expresses depth tonally, so --sh1/2/3 do not cross over and these do the work instead.
